text: 58-year-old male. The patient reports a year-long history of burning pain in his neck and arms, accompanying paresthesias in his hands. speaker: Doctor
text: Does the weakness or numbness affect your hands more than your feet, and have you noticed any difficulty with balance or walking? Also, have you experienced any changes in bowel or bladder control, such as incontinence or retention?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Burning pain in neck and arms, and weakness in both hands. I also have Paresthesias in hands, Absent reflexes, Decreased hand grip with fasciculations.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the combination of upper motor neuron signs like balance issues and lower motor neuron signs such as fasciculations and absent reflexes, I need to rule out structural compression first. REQUEST TEST: Cervical_Spine_MRI

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: A syrinx (cavity) within the spinal cord extending from the cervical to the upper thoracic region.

speaker: Doctor
text: The MRI confirms a syrinx, which explains the cape-like distribution of pain and the mixed upper and lower motor neuron signs. DIAGNOSIS READY: Syringomyelia
